Question B-007-004-009.

Why the correct answer is right: A wider signal occupies more frequency range, so different portions can fade differently. That makes selective fading more noticeable on wide bandwidths.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It is the same for both wide and narrow bandwidths": It is the same for both wide and narrow bandwidths ignores that a wider signal gives fading more spectrum to affect unevenly.
- sourceIndex 2: "Only the receiver bandwidth determines the selective fading effect": Only the receiver bandwidth determines the selective fading effect overlooks the transmitted signal bandwidth and propagation path.
- sourceIndex 3: "It is more pronounced at narrow bandwidths": It is more pronounced at narrow bandwidths reverses the usual effect; narrow signals are less likely to show frequency-selective distortion.
